## Discussion

<!-- ~12 lines. Close the project on substance, not summary:
     - the general message: a purely LOCAL quantum strategy, using only
       a node's degree and its neighbours' status, lowers the
       percolation threshold across ER, scale-free, small-world and a
       real WWW sample - in some cases by nearly an order of magnitude
       more than the honeycomb -> triangular result on lattices;
     - the trade-off: detached target nodes cap S~ below S even at
       p = 1, so gains in p_c are paid for in reachable fraction;
     - relevance for complex networks: quantum operations are a
       mechanism that *changes the topology itself*, which has no
       classical percolation analogue;
     - the average path length argument: log N in most complex networks
       versus N^{1/d} in d-dimensional lattices, so the probability of
       establishing entanglement decays linearly rather than
       exponentially in large finite networks;
     - limitations you did not address: noise and amplitude damping,
       multipartite strategies, global-knowledge protocols.
     One sentence, at most, connecting Part II back to Part I - the two
     projects are independent and the report should not pretend
     otherwise. -->
